confidence_why: One first-hand description of the tone system, checked against the source; 11 other works consulted do not discuss stress.

GEMA Online Journal of Language Studies 19(1):77-96.
tone_statements.quote: Menurut Court ( dalam Gandour 1979), kemasukan nada dalam bahasa Melayu terutama DST lebih kepada nada naik turun / / terutama di akhir suku kata yang terbuka. Manakala bagi nada tinggi / / di tempat-tempat lain. … Sementara bagi vokal panjang, bunyi aspirasi dan bernada tidak akan ditemui dalam DML. Mudahnya, ciri ini tiada pada DML. … Begitu juga bagi vokal panjang dan nada, kedua-duanya hadir pada bahasa Thai tetapi tidak pada DSL dan DST. Ini bermakna masyarakat Satun banyak meminjam leksikal dari Thai. Yang jelasnya, leksikal ini dipinjam bersama ciri fonologinya.
tone_statements.translation: According to Court (in Gandour 1979), the tone that enters Malay, especially DST [Thai Satun dialect], is mostly the rising-falling tone / ˆ/, especially on open final syllables, and the high tone / ´/ elsewhere. … As for long vowels, aspirated sounds and toned sounds, they will not be found in DML [Langkawi Malay dialect]. Simply, these features are absent in DML. … Likewise for long vowels and tone: both are present in Thai but not in DSL and DST. This means the Satun community borrows much lexicon from Thai. Clearly, this lexicon is borrowed together with its phonological features.
tone_statements.summary: No native lexical tone system: Thai loanwords keep their Thai tones (rising-falling on open final syllables, high elsewhere) and a handful of native words (air, ular) are said with tone by bilingual Satun speakers; authors state tone is a Thai feature not proper to Satun/Kedah Malay, though the abstract calls tone assignment a systematic process.

tone_statements.citation: Nor Hashimah Jalaluddin & Zaharani Ahmad. 2017. The Kedah Malay dialects spoken among Thai speakers in Langkawi and Satun: a preliminary study. Abstract, The Twenty-First International Symposium on Malay/Indonesian Linguistics (ISMIL 21), Langkawi, 4-6 May 2017. 1 p.
tone_statements.quote: More interestingly, Bankhuan, an interior village maintain the Kedah dialect but with a strong Thai accent. The variants of Kedah dialect is clearly indicated in their pronunciation. Phonologically - the tones (high-low, low-high, low – [...]), aspirated phonemes [kʰa...w], the monosyllabic words (lepat changed to pat), are distinctively found in this dialect.
tone_statements.summary: Claims contact-induced pitch patterns (high-low, low-high, low) in the Thai-accented Bankhuan variant of Kedah Malay; preliminary, no system described.

sources.note: Describes another variety. GIS dialect-geography paper on Thai Malay (Satun/Patani) influence in N. Malaysia; tone mentioned only for Thai and the Thai word [nɑ̂m] used in Padang Siding; nothing on Kedah Malay tone or stress.

tone.quote: Sementara penutur Thai menyebut ‘air’ dengan [ɑʲjɑʕ]. Adanya tambahan geluncuran /ʲ/ bagi perkataan air yang jelas boleh membezakan dengan penutur Thai. Kehadiran bunyi geluncuran ini ada kaitan dengan nada kerana bahasa Thai adalah bahasa bernada. Yang lebih menarik ada leksikal [nɑ̂m] yang bermaksud ‘air’ digunakan di Padang Siding. [nɑ̂m] adalah leksikal orang Thai sendiri. Perhatikan ada lambang [ ̂] iaitu nada tinggi rendah semasa menuturkan bunyi [nɑ̂m]. Ini memang ciri dari bahasa Thai (Gandeur, 1997).
tone.translation: Whereas the Thai speakers pronounce 'air' [water] as [ɑʲjɑʕ]. The added glide /ʲ/ in the word air clearly distinguishes the Thai speakers. The presence of this glide is connected with tone, because Thai is a tonal language. More interesting still, the lexical item [nɑ̂m] meaning 'water' is used in Padang Siding. [nɑ̂m] is the Thai people's own word. Note the symbol [ ̂], i.e. a high-low tone when pronouncing [nɑ̂m]. This is indeed a feature of Thai (Gandeur, 1997).
tone.summary: GIS dialect-geography paper on Thai Malay (Satun/Patani) influence in N. Malaysia; tone mentioned only for Thai and the Thai word [nɑ̂m] used in Padang Siding; nothing on Kedah Malay tone or stress.
tone.says: GIS dialect-geography paper on Thai Malay (Satun/Patani) influence in N. Malaysia; tone mentioned only for Thai and the Thai word [nɑ̂m] used in Padang Siding; nothing on Kedah Malay tone or stress.
